theme: World reacts to the player: NPCs report crimes, judge appearance and reputation
reviews: 5 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; GamesRadar; Tom's Guide; TechRadar; Windows Central
test: Wear a worker's coat in one scene and a smart suit in the next; the same named person greets him differently by regard, and a witnessed theft is reported by that witness to a third person who then acts on it.

theme: Quests and jobs solvable several ways
reviews: 6 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; GamesRadar; Game Informer; Tom's Guide; TechRadar; Windows Central
test: Take one break-in job three times (sneak in, talk in, pay a key-holder); all three complete the job with different later consequences and none is flagged as the wrong route.

theme: Melee combat reads and rewards learning (directional, counters)
reviews: 6 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; Game Informer; Tom's Guide; TechRadar; Windows Central; Windows Central roundup (IGN, Dexerto, VideoGamer, GamesHub)
test: In a scripted fight against a known fighter type, a tester who learns his tell and answers it wins hurt; one who ignores it loses; two fresh testers report the tell was readable.
note: LEDGER is street fists, not swords; same principle of readable blows.

theme: Combat stiff, imprecise targeting, messy group fights
reviews: 2 of 6+roundup: GamesRadar; TechRadar
test: In a three-against-one fight, Tom can pick and change who he is facing without lock-on and without the camera or targeting fighting him; blows land or miss visibly in under 100 ms of input.
note: Game Informer also found some fights unfair (3 of 6 in all).

theme: Slow, punishing early hours; patience required; steep learning curve
reviews: 5 of 6+roundup: GamesRadar; Game Informer; Tom's Guide; TechRadar; Windows Central roundup (IGN, Dexerto, VideoGamer, GamesHub)
test: A new tester with no briefing reaches a first earned payment and a first witnessed consequence inside the first hour without asking for help.

theme: Saving restricted (potion needed) - major annoyance
reviews: 1 of 6+roundup: TechRadar
test: Quit the game at any moment mid-street and mid-job; the next launch resumes at that moment with nothing lost and no item or cost needed to save.

theme: Stealth is the weakest part of play
reviews: 1 of 6+roundup: Game Informer
test: A tester told only 'get past the watcher unseen' can do it using a doorway or unlit stretch and standing still, and the watcher's reaction matches the light on Tom.

theme: Stable, near bug-free on PC at launch
reviews: 3 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; TechRadar; Windows Central
test: The AI tester walks the packaged release build for an evening of play with no crash, no stuck state and no blocked job.

theme: Occasional glitches, a quest blocked then auto-failed
reviews: 3 of 6+roundup: GamesRadar; TechRadar; Windows Central
test: Force a job step to become impossible (target moved, door locked); the job moves to a named soft-fail state, tells Tom in plain words, and never fails silently.

theme: Menus/subtitles with typos, map crowded with icons, hard-to-read dialogue options
reviews: 3 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; TechRadar; Windows Central
test: Read every menu, subtitle and talk option in a full pass: zero typos, the paper map shows no quest icons, and each spoken option's tone matches what Tom then says.

theme: Voice acting uneven; secondary characters flat
reviews: 3 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; Tom's Guide; Windows Central
test: Play lines from all thirty regulars and crowd voices to a fresh listener; no voice is marked flat, odd-stressed or off-accent for its casting sheet.

theme: Hunger, sleep and spoiling food: another meter to tend
reviews: 1 of 6+roundup: TechRadar
test: Play a week with no bars on screen; Tom's tiredness or hunger shows in his body and talk only, and no tester reports a chore to keep him fed.
note: Tom's Guide praised the same systems for roleplay (mixed).

theme: Consequences softened, choices lack weight
reviews: 1 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer
test: After a witnessed serious deed, a mark stays on the town (a person who will not serve him, a notice, a charge) a week of game time later.

theme: Historical authenticity and a believable, beautiful world
reviews: 5 of 6+roundup: GamesRadar; Game Informer; Tom's Guide; TechRadar; Windows Central
test: A reviewer with Hook sheet and period photographs finds no anachronism in a walked 1990 street and can name the era from the street alone.

theme: Strong story, characters and writing
reviews: 5 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; GamesRadar; Game Informer; Tom's Guide; Windows Central
test: A tester can describe one named person's wants and why Tom should be honest with him after a single evening, without being told.

theme: Side activities and emergent small moments
reviews: 3 of 6+roundup: PC Gamer; Game Informer; Tom's Guide
test: In one evening of free play, a tester names two unprompted moments they would retell, and neither was a main job.

theme: Climax rushed; some main sections force a playstyle
reviews: 2 of 6+roundup: Game Informer; Tom's Guide
test: Act III keeps the same number of open routes per job as Act II, and the final stretch is timed within the hour budget with no step marked forced.

theme: Heist planning and execution is the highlight
reviews: 4 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; PCGamesN; The Guardian (via inkl); WeGotThisCovered
test: A break-in is cased in advance, a plan chosen, then carried out; the case changes at least one thing the job needs, and the outcome differs with the plan.
note: Two of four praised the online co-op heists; LEDGER has no online.

theme: Missions restart or fail for small deviations; stalemates
reviews: 2 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; PCGamesN
test: Tom kills a target early, arrives late or leaves the route; the job continues in a changed state rather than a fail-and-reload screen.
note: Also criticised in RDR2 reviews (see rdr2 rigid missions).

theme: Three playable leads, Trevor and Michael praised
reviews: 2 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; The Guardian (via inkl)
note: LEDGER has one protagonist, Tom; the closest answer is the crew and the thirty regulars (2.11, 3.2.3), not alternate leads. Design choice, not fault.

theme: Characters overshadowed by the world, contradict motives to suit missions, story aimless
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; The Guardian (via inkl); CGMagazine
test: Take each principal through three jobs; in every scene what he does follows his stated temper and want, and a tester can state what Act II is about in one sentence.

theme: Dense, detailed, physical world
reviews: 5 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; PCGamesN; The Guardian (via inkl); CGMagazine; GameSpot roundup (Metro, USgamer, Kotaku, VideoGamer)
test: A tester walking Quay Street at dawn and at dusk lists small details unprompted that were not on the Hook sheet.

theme: Satire and humour (wears thin, heavy-handed, silly puns)
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: PCGamesN; CGMagazine; GameSpot
note: No LEDGER part is about satire; it is a period crime drama. Closest is street lines (3.6.4) but tone is not specified as satire.

theme: Shooting and cover system weak
reviews: 2 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; PCGamesN
test: Firearms appear only at the dial's top; in those scenes Tom cannot trade shots from cover at will, and no mission requires a firefight to proceed.
note: LEDGER is not gun-heavy by design.

theme: Driving too sensitive, hard in chases; vehicles distinct
reviews: 1 of 5+roundup: GameSpot
test: A tester drives a chase with keyboard and pad; the car stays controllable at speed and a first-time driver stays on the road for a full lap.

theme: Police chase and wanted levels intense
reviews: 1 of 5+roundup: GameSpot
test: After a witnessed deed, police response climbs in named steps and falls again with time and distance, and a tester can say what step it is at from what he sees.

theme: Radio, soundtrack, custom music
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: PCGamesN; CGMagazine; WeGotThisCovered
test: Tune the car radio through a full day; each station's programme is period-correct and Pauline's radio is not repeated within an hour.

theme: Menus cumbersome, long loading
reviews: 2 of 5+roundup: PCGamesN; GameSpot roundup (Metro, USgamer, Kotaku, VideoGamer)
test: From main menu to Tom on the street in under the stated loading budget; any menu item is reached in three presses or fewer.

theme: Smooth 60 fps, strong graphics options, but heavy at max settings
reviews: 5 of 5+roundup: PCGamesN; The Guardian (via inkl); WeGotThisCovered; CGMagazine; GameSpot
test: Packaged build on a mid-range reference PC holds the frame target for a walk and a drive with no shader hitch; display options change visibly.

theme: First-person mode
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; PCGamesN; GameSpot roundup (Metro, USgamer, Kotaku, VideoGamer)
note: LEDGER's camera is third person, on-foot follow at fixed range (1.1.2); no first-person mode is planned.

theme: Rockstar Editor and Director Mode
reviews: 4 of 5+roundup: PCGamesN; The Guardian (via inkl); WeGotThisCovered; CGMagazine
test: Photo mode opens at any calm moment, hides the HUD, and saves a full-size image the tester can open outside the game.
note: Video editing is not in LEDGER; photo mode only.

theme: GTA Online (lag, variety, heists)
reviews: 4 of 5+roundup: PCGamesN; The Guardian (via inkl); WeGotThisCovered; GameSpot roundup (Metro, USgamer, Kotaku, VideoGamer)
note: LEDGER is single-player only; out of scope.

theme: Little new for returning players; high price
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: PCGamesN; CGMagazine; WeGotThisCovered
test: A free demo covers the first hour so a buyer can judge value before paying.
note: Weak mapping; value is a store matter.

theme: Story missions scripted, punish deviation, force violence
reviews: 4 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; bit-tech; GameSpot; GameSpot roundup (Eurogamer, IGN, Guardian, GamesRadar, Game Informer, USgamer)
test: Repeat one job leaving the 'intended' route; it continues with a changed state in 4 of 5 deviations tried, never an instant fail screen.
note: GameSpot roundup also names predictable mission structure.

theme: Mission structure predictable and drags mid-game
reviews: 2 of 5+roundup: GameSpot; GameSpot roundup (Eurogamer, IGN, Guardian, GamesRadar, Game Informer, USgamer)
test: Across a week, no two consecutive jobs share the same step template and a tester names three different verbs used.

theme: Story and characters, Arthur and gang
reviews: 4 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; bit-tech; GameSpot; GameSpot roundup (Eurogamer, IGN, Guardian, GamesRadar, Game Informer, USgamer)
test: A tester names every member of the firm and says what each wants after a week.

theme: World detail and reactive towns and NPCs
reviews: 4 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; bit-tech; GameSpot; GameZone
test: Spill, break or leave something in a street; within the hour bystanders react and the thing is still there or visibly dealt with.

theme: Honor system and reactive greetings
reviews: 1 of 5+roundup: GameSpot
test: Raise and lower Tom's name by deeds; the same named person's greeting changes in words and manner, and no number is shown.

theme: Eating and weight system intrusive
reviews: 1 of 5+roundup: GameSpot
test: A week of play requires no eating chore; Tom's state shows only in body and talk.
note: GameZone praised the survival systems as adding depth (mixed).

theme: Heavy movement, many bindings, context inputs, steep learning curve
reviews: 2 of 5+roundup: Windows Central; GameZone
test: A tester uses only walk, run, one action key and talk for the first hour; any extra control is taught in play with no manual.

theme: Crashes at launch, launcher problems
reviews: 5 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; bit-tech; GameSpot; Windows Central; GameZone
test: Fresh PC, install, launch and play without any account or captcha step beyond the store, no crash in a one-hour walk.

theme: Settings list overwhelming, many with little effect
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; GameZone; Windows Central
test: The options screen has no more than a stated short list, each with a visible preview, and a default preset fits a mid-range PC.

theme: Photo mode
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; Windows Central; GameZone
test: Photo mode opens at one key, hides the HUD, offers depth of field and saves a local image.

theme: Best-looking game, lighting and detail
reviews: 5 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; bit-tech; GameSpot; Windows Central; GameZone
test: Hook sheet and period photograph comparison of dawn, dusk and night frames shows no visible fault or placeholder.

theme: Random encounters and optional stories reward exploration
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; bit-tech; GameSpot
test: A tester walking without a job meets a street happening within ten minutes at three of four times of day.

theme: Auto-lock aim makes stealth unappealing; limited choice
reviews: 1 of 5+roundup: GameSpot
test: Tom can avoid a fight by using light or leaving, and no job forces violence to continue.

theme: Core combat shallow over long campaign
reviews: 1 of 5+roundup: bit-tech
test: A tester lists at least four distinct ways a street fight can start or end (talk down, run, hurt one, police arrive).

theme: Limited fast travel, slow methodical pace, 40-60 hours
reviews: 3 of 5+roundup: PC Gamer; bit-tech; GameSpot
test: Time can be skipped by waiting or taking a ride, and no walk between two regular places exceeds the stated minutes.

theme: Emotional tension, known outcome
reviews: 2 of 5+roundup: bit-tech; GameSpot
test: A tester at the start of Act III can predict some ending signs, and rates them as dread not spoiler.
note: Weak mapping: LEDGER is not a prequel.
